Another source told Page Six reflected on how much Teresa adores Milania, which makes the most recent incident “heartbreaking.”
“Teresa’s like a great mom,” the insider said. “She’s calm. She’s cool. She’s supportive, despite all the millions of hours she’s had to work and all the money she brings in. She’s such a good mom to those girls.”
A rep for Milania told Page Six , “Milania is deeply loved by her family and friends, and all of us are doing everything we can to support her as she navigates an incredibly difficult time in her life, particularly following the devastating loss of her best friend, Victoria.
“She is currently surrounded by people who love her and is under the care of professionals who are working with her and her family.”
The statement continued that Milania is a “good-hearted and caring young woman who has been going through a very challenging period.”
Her rep ended, “…Our focus right now is simply on her health, healing and well-being. In time, she hopes that being open about her experiences may help other young people facing their own struggles, but for now, we ask for compassion and privacy as she and her family continue to navigate this together.”
This isn’t the first time Milania has had a run-in with law enforcement this year.
On May 14, she was arrested for domestic violence and simple assault after she allegedly struck and caused bodily harm to an individual with the initials “LR.” She entered a not guilty plea and enrolled in anger management classes.
Another source close to the family said that Milania has had her own rough waters to navigate lately.
The insider pointed to Milania losing her best friend Victoria Zardoya to an accident in July, her father living in the Bahamas and growing up in the spotlight as contributing factors.
Despite Milania’s recent struggles, Joe Giudice, 56, who has not been back to the United States after being deported in Oct. 2019 , told Page Six he has his daughter’s back .
“Milania is a good girl. She has a big heart, she loves deeply, and she cares enormously about the people in her life. She is also young and going through a very difficult period right now,” Joe said through his rep at Dominton Talent House.
“The loss of her close friend Victoria in July affected Milania tremendously. Losing someone you love is incredibly painful, and grief does not have a timeline. She has been trying to process that loss while also dealing with the pressures that come with growing up in the public eye.”
He continued, “As her father, my priority is making sure my daughter knows that she is loved and supported. Our family is doing everything we can to be there for her and give her the support and space she needs right now.”
Joe went on to ask for compassion for Milania and to reserve judgment, and to “remember that you do not know everything someone may be carrying behind closed doors.”
“She deserves love, understanding and privacy as she works through everything she has been experiencing.”
“I love my daughter, and I will always stand beside her.”

articles.content_orig:
American businesses ramped up orders for Chinese goods in the weeks leading up to the high-stakes summit this week, as companies positioned for continued stability between the world's two largest economies.
The jump in orders was a "surprise," with shipments to the U.S. rising on both a yearly and monthly basis "as China's relative tariff position improved," according to China Beige Book, a New York-based research firm that surveyed 1,295 Chinese companies between Sept. 1-22.
The gauge measuring orders from the U.S. — calculated as the proportion of surveyed firms reporting an increase minus the share reporting a decrease — jumped to 13 in September, from negative-12 a year earlier and 3 in August, according to the report.
Even so, overall Chinese domestic and export orders remained below their levels a year earlier, and new orders weakened from August, the report showed.
The upswing in U.S.-bound orders came as businesses positioned for a friendlier outcome at the summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping , who is in Washington this week for his first state visit in more than a decade.
The two countries agreed to extend by two months to January a trade truce that keeps tariffs lower, suspends restrictive controls on rare earth exports and holds off higher port fees on ships.
The U.S. also reportedly planned to delay a threatened round of tariffs tied to industrial overcapacity until at least after this week's summit, easing near-term pressure on Chinese exporters.
The effective U.S. tariff rate on Chinese goods of around 23% remains well above the average levy the U.S. imposes on other major trading partners, according to Barclays.
The export order figures align with recent official data that showed China's ports saw their busiest week on record in the run-up to the summit , another sign that trade flows were recovering amid hopes for a further thaw in bilateral relations.
Following the truce extension, Eurasia Group raised its odds of continued stability in the bilateral relationship to the highest level since Trump returned to office. The shorter-than-expected extension of the truce is also unlikely to reignite tensions, the consultancy firm said.
"Neither government has an interest in renewed escalation," said Dan Wang, China director at Eurasia Group, who expects both sides to press each other for near-term commitments to maintain the fragile stability.
Washington is likely to seek further progress on expedited Chinese approval of rare-earth export licenses for U.S. end users, as well as increased purchases of U.S. agricultural goods, Wang said, and in return, Beijing would expect the White House to maintain its current pause on arms sales to Taiwan.
The two leaders are expected to meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, and potentially on the sidelines of the G20 summit the U.S. is hosting in Miami in December. No bilateral meeting after this week's summit has been confirmed.

After a tough Week 1, we got back on track in Week 2. That's good news. As I said at the start of the week, the more we find out about these teams, the better we get (hopefully).
Stefon Diggs hit his five receptions, Jordan Love threw a pair of touchdowns to cash that bet, and the Rams won on "Monday Night Football." I had tied that to an any-time Puka Nacua touchdown, but Nacua didn't play (this column comes out on Friday, and last Friday, his status was up in the air). Hopefully you tailed the Los Angeles pick at least.
Regarding the misses, the Eagles , as seven-point favorites, barely escaped the Titans . Saquon Barkley getting hurt and missing a significant amount of the game didn't help, but clearly I underestimated Tennessee, and I also underestimated how much the Philadelphia offensive line and running game is struggling. I also missed on Justin Jefferson 80+ receiving yards. The game was took place in an absolute downpour. Sometimes, that's just how it goes.
Again, more knowledge is good. Week 2 was better than Week 1. Let's make Week 3 better than Week 2. As always, odds are via DraftKings .
Let's do a quick rundown of what the Commanders are facing:
Need I say more? I'd be surprised if the Commanders keep this within single digits, so if you want an alternate line, be my guest. I'll stick with Seattle -7.5 here.
Jameson Williams has to get going at some point, right? He has just six catches for 78 yards through two weeks, and his longest catch is just 22 yards. That's not the Jameson Williams we've come to know. He's a big play waiting to happen, and we shouldn't have to wait much longer.
This week will be the week it happens. The Jets ' defense has impressed thus far, but it helped that they played the Titans and then faced the Packers in the pouring rain. In the safe confines of Ford Field, the Lions -- and especially Williams -- are set to have a big day. Plus, given the state of the Lions' defense, this could be a high-scoring game that forces both offenses to keep their foot on the gas pedal.
Williams is still seeing solid under-the-hood numbers. He has 13 targets, and he's playing 90% of Detroit's offensive snaps. Two drops early have hurt, but Jared Goff sung his praises this offseason. He averaged 67 receiving yards per game in 2024 and 66 last year. Coming off a mini-bye, the Lions will have some big opportunities dialed up for their speedster.
Bryce Young has been superb to start this season, but check these numbers out:
Guess who plays the most man coverage in the NFL by a wide margin? The Browns !
It's a small sample size, of course, but Young also struggled vs. man coverage last year. There are concerns about whether Jalen Coker can play, too, and the ground game is yet to get going.
Meanwhile, I'm not buying the Deshaun Watson one-game renaissance. If he plays poorly at home, the boo birds will come out quickly, and it could snowball in the wrong direction from there. Carolina's defense played much better in Week 2, and it should be able to do so again here.
The Chargers ' offense has been an absolute mess this year. If you want a breakdown of why it's bad and how it can be fixed , JP Acosta explained it earlier today.
But the defense has also been underwhelming, and it's facing the Bills ' excellent offense. You know what that means? The Chargers will be chasing points all day long.
Ladd McConkey has been one of the very, very few bright spots. Not only has he looked good, but the Chargers' offense has actually looked good when he's on the field. No, really!
Anyway, McConkey has been a full participant in practice this week after leaving Week 1 with a rib injury and being questionable entering Week 2. He should have a big day.
I love combining these two here for a solid payout. New Orleans is coming off a 24-17 win over the Raiders . In the fourth quarter this season, Tyler Shough is 24 for 31 (77.4% comp pct) for 271 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions.
Plus, I don't think we're giving this Saints defense enough credit. Maybe it's because of their history with previous teams, but former Chargers coach Brandon Staley has been terrific as New Orleans' defensive coordinator, and the same goes for former No. 2 overall pick Chase Young . Since the start of last season, the Saints are 11th in defensive EPA per play. Young had 10 sacks in just 12 games last year and is off to another terrific start. His 18% pressure rate is 10th among 94 players with at least 40 pass rush snaps.
And then there's Chris Olave , who is just so, so good. He's seen 23 targets through two weeks and has 18 catches. He can win all over the field, and his route running is superb. The Raiders' secondary has been one of the pleasant surprises early this year, but they've yet to see a player of this caliber. Olave should have another huge day.

articles.title_orig: Trump and Xi exchange warm words at state dinner but little progress on key issues
articles.title_zh: Trump and Xi exchange warm words at state dinner but little progress on key issues
articles.content_orig:
Watch: The worldâs two most powerful men just met. How did it go?
US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping exchanged warm words at a lavish White House state dinner but gave little indication of progress on pressing issues.
Xi stressed that they should ensure AI remain "under human control" and act "as responsible major countries", while Trump toasted a future of "harmony, peace and success" for both nations.
But tensions remain despite the diplomatic niceties, including over Taiwan - with Xi urging Trump earlier in the day to take the "correct position" on the self-governing island which Beijing claims, amid a weapons package paused by Trump.
Billionaire business leaders and US tech CEOs joined the leaders at the extravagant dinner late on Thursday.
Their arrival was marked by protesters shouting from just outside the White House gates, some of whom were arrested.
Trump lavished praise on Xi during his first visit to the US in over a decade, telling those attending the dinner that while the two countries had "different systems", they had "never gotten along better".
Xi meanwhile welcomed the "historic juncture" in US-China relations - and said both leaders' ambitions could "surely be mutually reinforcing".
"China and the United States must act as responsible major countries to meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other," he said.
While Xi said he and Trump had shared "in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues", little mention was made of the crucial matters which divide the leaders of the world's two most powerful countries.
China believes the US is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way - particularly when it comes to trade, technology and Taiwan.
Trump has meanwhile been expected to aim for deals around trade and tariffs during the visit â like lowering Chinese tariffs on American goods, increasing imports of Chinese rare earth minerals, and increasing exports of US agricultural products.
Xi thanked his hosts for receiving him and his wife with "meticulous care and consideration"
Trump has been blunt about his ambitions for artificial intelligence (AI) - and clear that he considers China to be the US's main rival for its development.
But beyond Xi's reference to AI remaining under "human control", little indication was given of what progress the two leaders may have made on the issue during their talks.
The dinner also came just hours after Chinese state media reported Xi had, behind closed doors, advised Washington to handle "with prudence" its approach to Taiwan. Washington is yet to comment publicly on the remarks.
The US is legally bound to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but Trump delayed approving a $14bn (Â£11bn) arms package for it after Xi in May warned that mishandling the issue could cause the two countries to "collide or even enter into conflict".
At the time, Trump called it a "very good negotiating chip" with Beijing.
Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far
Trump and Xi come face-to-face as US and China battle to win the AI race
Xi got Trump's red carpet welcome - but not everything he wanted
The evening marked a continuation of the lavish welcome Xi has so far received in the US.
Trump presented the Chinese president with a sculpture of a bald eagle - America's national symbol - saying it embodied "the free and soaring spirit of America". First Lady Melania had participated in its design, Trump added.
Others in attendance included key White House figures, such as Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, chief of staff Monica Crowley, and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.
They were joined by scores of US officials, as well as conservative broadcasters, tech industry bosses, social media CEOs and corporate executives.
Apple's Tim Cook and Nvidia's Jensen Huang were seated at the same table as Trump and Xi, as was Elon Musk, who previously worked in Trump's administration leading the effort to shrink government.
OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google's Sundar Pichai, and Amazon's Jeff Bezos were also present, as were Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Yass, the American billionaire who owns a share of TikTok.
Musk was seen mingling with guests, alongside US Secretary of State Marco Rubio
The leaders of companies including General Motors, Visa, Paramount Skydance and ExxonMobil could also be seen in the room.
"Everybody wanted to be there," Trump said ahead of the event. "I would say you have the entire tech world, the entire banking world, and a lot more."
One notable absence was Anthropic - one of the biggest and most valuable AI firms in the world. The BBC has asked Anthropic if it was invited, or if they chose not to be there.
Business leaders and tech bosses were among those in attendance
The office of the First Lady Melania Trump, which planned the event, said the dinner menu would showcase "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence".
The first course was yellow squash, wild mushrooms and crispy pancetta. The guests ate off red tablecloths - red being a symbol of luck and good fortune in China.
For their main course they dined on a sesame-crusted sea bass, braised bok choy and roasted eggplant.
Dessert featured the two leaders and their fellow diners tucking into vanilla crÃ©meux with sour cherry confit, with an accompanying ice cream "made with harvested White House honey".
The wine chosen by the first lady included Schramsberg Blanc De Noir - a nod to President Nixon's 1972 "Toast to Peace" with former Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai, when they used a bottle from the same vineyard.
Watch: Trump puts on a warm reception for Xi in Washington
Trump and Xi will begin the final day of their visit on Friday with tea at the White House's Red Room with their wives.
The group will then head to the US National Archives for a tour of the building and its exhibits.
Formally called the National Archives and Records Administration, the building holds some of the most important documents regarding the founding of the United States - including the US Constitution, the Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights.
Xi and his wife will depart Washington later in the day.

Oooh, that unmatched satisfaction of peeling a perfectly printed label or sticker and slapping it on your water bottle, food container or whatever else is close by! If anyone knows what I'm talking about, this one's for you – the crafting giant Cricut is taking the joy of label and high-end sticker making to the next level with two new machines: the Cricut StickerPix Print and the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut .
Available now, both models could easily hit our lists of the best label makers , or the best laminators . But they're so much more than that. They serve as compact mini-print shops that print and laminate pro-quality, water- and scratch-resistant stickers and photos using ultra-vivid 300 DPI dye-sublimation technology.
That may be a mouthful, but it basically means these are very capable little things. The standard Cricut StickerPix Print (£159.99 for the Essential Bundle) works seamlessly with pre-cut sticker sheets—perfect for quick, uniform labels. Meanwhile, the advanced Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut (£249.99 for the Essential Bundle) adds a built-in cutter, automatically kiss-cutting custom shapes directly around your unique designs. Both connect effortlessly to the free Cricut Design Space app, meaning you can transform your smartphone photos and designs into tactile stickers in minutes.
The Cricut StickerPix Print Essential Bundle has everything you'll need. It includes the machine, an ink cartridge (54 prints), 18 circle pre-cut sticker sheets, 18 rectangle pre-cut sticker sheets, 18 glossy photo papers, a power adapter, and a material tray. Perfect for beginner crafters.
At $299, the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut Essential Bundle equips you for custom sticker projects instantly. Included alongside the machine is an ink cartridge (36 prints), 18 glossy sticker sheets, 18 photo paper sheets, a pre-installed cutting tool, material tray, power adapter, and a free Cricut Access trial subscription.
So, who's this for? Well, everyone from label/sticker homebody maniacs to digital artists and small business owners.
If you run a market stall or Etsy shop, the StickerPix Print could be a really nice addition to your business. It’s efficient for batch-printing logos, price tags, QR codes, or packaging seals using the pre-cut circular and rectangular sheets. And, because the dye-sublimation prints come out completely dry and laminated, you won't have to worry about smudging labels. It's also ideal for anyone who wants to label their spice jars or craft room storage without fussing over intricate cuts.
I think there's also scope for illustrators to use these things, especially those who want to share their art at conventions – after all, everyone loves stickers! You can upload a hand-drawn illustration or a photo from your phone, and the machine will print, laminate, and precisely kiss-cut a custom border around the image so the backing stays intact for easy peeling.
For me, I'm excited to use them to create unique water bottle sticks and fun gifts for my son's birthday party bags.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo XIV begins historic 4-day visit to France
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo XIV begins historic 4-day visit to France
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo arrived in France on Friday, Sept. 25, starting a four-day tour across Paris, Lourdes, and Metz that includes speeches and a massive outdoor mass. (HOST BROADCASTER via Reuters.)
Pope Leo XIV began his visit to France on Friday for his fifth Apostolic Journey as Pontiff. The four-day trip marks the first formal papal visit to the country once called "the eldest daughter of the Church" since Pope Benedict XVI’s visit in September 2008.
French bishops announced the visit’s theme as "That the world may have life," and it comes as the officially secular nation is seeing an influx of new baptisms. So far this year, according to the Conference of Bishops of France, more than 21,000 adults have joined the Church, an increase driven by 18 to 25-year-olds.
"Pope Leo's visit to France has sparked a real tidal wave" of interest, retired French Bishop Marc Stenger told Reuters. "French Catholics are… saying ​loudly that they need the Church to find their way in these uncertain moments in world history."
POPE LEO WARNS AI RISKS BECOMING TOOL OF 'DOMINATION, EXCLUSION AND DEATH' IN NEW ENCYCLICAL
The pope will visit Metz on Sept. 28, 2026 to conclude his four-day state and pastoral trip to France, which also includes stops in Paris and Lourdes. (Jean-Christophe Verhaegen / AFP via Getty Images)
The rise comes after a 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades, and said the Church had shown "deep, total and even cruel indifference" ​to victims. Stenger, who led the Diocese of Troyes from 1999 to 2020, told Reuters the scandals "have deeply wounded the Church and damaged its credibility."
In what is described as an unusual move, the Vatican press office announced Pope Leo will meet privately in Lourdes with seven of those victims as part of a message of healing and vulnerability.
SAN FRANCISCO ARCHDIOCESE AGREES TO $395M SETTLEMENT WITH 530 CLERGY ABUSE SURVIVORS
The Vatican calls the trip, "a journey that unites faith and public engagement, memory and the future, with listening and bridge-building at its heart." After being greeted by French President Emmanuel Macron and a courtesy visit to Élysée Palace on Friday, Pope Leo is scheduled to make 15 speeches during his visit. He is expected to speak on several spiritual and societal themes, including the need to protect immigrants , the sick and unborn, and defend human dignity in the era of AI, and address themes of peace, culture, and unity.
President of France Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron welcome Pope Leo XIV to Élysée Palace on Sept. 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Tom Nicholson/Getty Images)
French bishops have expressed surprise at the level of interest in the visit. The Associated Press reports organizers for Pope Leo’s Saturday Mass at Paris’ Place de la Concorde, expecting up to 1 million people, have lengthened the security perimeter, extending the site beyond the 1.2-mile length of the Champs-Élysées, where Pope Leo will parade in the Popemobile.
Among his more noteworthy stops, Pope Leo will worship and speak on Sunday at the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes, one of Christianity’s most-visited pilgrimage destinations, especially popular with the sick. It is where an ailing Pope John Paul II , on his final foreign trip in 2004, delivered a forceful condemnation of abortion and euthanasia.
Pope Leo XIV attends the Welcome Ceremony at Paris Orly International Airport on Sept. 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Simone Risoluti - Vatican Media via Vatican Pool/Getty Images)
Pope Leo’s visit, however, comes after France’s recent national debate and subsequent passage of legislation allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication. That followed 2024 legislation enshrining abortion as a constitutional right .
POPE LEO PROMOTES ARCHBISHOP WHO BARRED PELOSI FROM COMMUNION TO ONE OF VATICAN'S HIGHEST COURTS
On Friday, Pope Leo will speak at the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, or UNESCO, headquarters in Paris. Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni says Leo will likely reiterate his call for an AI slowdown and speak "with regard to the meaning of existence, to what makes human beings human and what does not."
The speech comes after the Pope’s May manifesto in which Leo warned of the dangers of AI and urged international regulation of the industry. His position again puts him at odds with President Trump, who has encouraged AI innovation so the U.S. can compete with and surpass China.
A crucifix stands in front of the Basilique Notre-Dame du Rosaire, its spire draped with a banner marking the upcoming visit of Pope Leo XIV, five days ahead of the pontiff's trip to the site as part of his apostolic journey to France, in Lourdes on Sept. 22, 2026.
Following his UNESCO visit, Pope Leo holds a prayer service at the newly-restored Cathedral of Notre-Dame, marking the first papal visit since a 2019 fire nearly destroyed one of France’s national landmarks.
He concludes his trip on Monday with a symbolic full-day visit to the border city of Metz, the birthplace of former French Prime Minister Robert Schuman, considered one of the founding fathers of the European Union. It is a backdrop the Vatican says the Pope will use to "champion friendship among European peoples."

French Ambassador to the Vatican Charles Personnaz told Reuters that Macron has invited leaders from all 27 EU members to attend the speech and meet with the Pontiff. Other media reports say Ukrainian President V olodymyr Zelenskyy may also attend.
Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: The drones Russia could strike Europe with from Mediterranean fleet
articles.title_zh: The drones Russia could strike Europe with from Mediterranean fleet
articles.content_orig:
After more than four years of war between Russia and Ukraine, technology and spending on military equipment have evolved significantly.
A number of Russian drones have been detected flying over European Union territory. There have been incursions into Poland and Bulgaria although, according to a CIA report, the situation could become more complicated.
The latest information from the CIA has made it clear that there is a risk of Russian drone attacks on Spain, France or Italy launched from containers on ships belonging to the shadow fleet in the Mediterranean. So, what kind of drones is the Russian army using? According to the latest information from the Ukrainian military, it goes far beyond the use of Iranian-made Shahed drones.
In the early hours of 27 August, Ukrainian air defences shot down or neutralised 233 Russian targets in a single night-time bombardment. Among them were 258 attack drones, two Oniks anti-ship missiles and several Iskander-M and KN-23 ballistic missiles.
According to the Ukrainian Air Force, around a third of those drones are jet-powered, while the rest are a mix of Shahed-type drones, Gerbera systems and Banderol missiles, as well as decoys.
That mix gives a fairly accurate picture of the state of Russia’s unmanned arsenal at this stage of the war: it is no longer based on a single model but on a whole family of systems performing different roles, from flooding the sky with cheap swarms to punching through at more than 500 kilometres per hour.
Part of the explanation lies in cost. Firing a million-dollar interceptor at a drone worth between €25,000-40,000 (€21,000-35,000) is unsustainable in the long run and that imbalance is precisely what Moscow is exploiting by launching waves capable of exhausting far more expensive air-defence systems with its drones, as well as with more conventional weapons.
The bulk of this drone fleet comes from the Alabuga Special Economic Zone in Tatarstan, some 1,200 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. The complex covers more than 2.8 million square metres and it is estimated that around 15% of its facilities are devoted, directly or indirectly, to war production.
There, composite fuselages are moulded, engines are manufactured, onboard electronics are assembled and completed parts are stored.
Ukrainian strikes on the complex have forced Russia to move much of that chain underground.
A Ukrainian open-source analyst estimates that around 42,000 square metres of underground space have already been built at Alabuga, the equivalent of six football pitches.
According to Russian media cited by 'The Economist', daily production of Geran-2 drones already exceeds 100 units, with plans to reach 500 a day. Geran-2 drones are the systems better known as the Shahed-136.
In terms of overall volume, estimates vary by source but point in the same direction. The Centre for Strategic and International Studies calculated that in March 2026 Russia was producing around 5,500 drones a month, while Ukrainian military intelligence put August output at around 3,000 Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones and some 2,800 Geran-2 a month.
In March of that same year, according to a report cited by Euronews, Russia had launched 6,462 Shahed-type drones and related attack and decoy systems, of which 4,186 were Shahed-type Geran-2 attack drones, an average of 208 launches a day – a pace that on some days rose to more than 900 drones .
This is the model that has underpinned most attacks since 2022. Designed in Iran, Russia manufactures its own version at Alabuga under the Geran-2 designation.
As Ukrainian interceptors have improved, Russia has been replacing propellers with jet engines. The leap has taken place in three stages.
The first, the Geran-3, based on the Shahed-238, reused the Geran-2 fuselage with an added turbojet. It reached speeds of between 300 and 370 km/h and had an operational range of close to 1,000 kilometres, with a combined thermal and fragmentation warhead of around 50 kilograms.
Ukrainian intelligence documented dozens of foreign components in its wreckage, many of them from US manufacturers, as well as Chinese and European parts.
The Geran-4 followed with an entirely redesigned fuselage rather than a simple adaptation. Its dimensions remain similar to those of the original Shahed – about 3.5 metres long with a 3-metre wingspan – but with integrated fixed wings to reduce drag.
According to specialist analysis, it cruises at between 300-350 km/h, with peaks of up to 500 km/h, flies at 4,000 to 5,000 metres and delivers a 50-kilogram warhead at a range of between 450 and 850 kilometres.
In practice, however, Russia has managed to stretch that figure: flying at high altitude to cut fuel consumption, a Geran-4 recorded a flight of around 960 kilometres on 28 August 2026, a distance that brings almost the whole of Ukrainian territory within range. Its cost is put at between $85,000-120,000 (€74,000-105,000) per unit.
The Geran-5 is the most recent variant. According to an analysis by the International Institute for Strategic Studies, it can reach up to 600 km/h, has a range of about 950 kilometres and a payload of around 90 kilograms; German-made transistors have been found in its remains . Both models are powered by the TF-TJ2000A engine.
The impact on Ukrainian defences has been significant. In March 2026 Ukraine was intercepting more than 90% of the drones launched against its territory ; by June, with Geran jet drones deployed on a large scale, that rate had fallen to just over 50%. Kyiv responded with its own jet-powered interceptors, such as the Alexa Spatium, which entered service on 21 August 2026.
Originally conceived as a cheap decoy to saturate radar screens alongside real Geran-2 drones, the Gerbera model has been steadily gaining its own offensive capability.
Unlike the Shahed and Geran drones, designed for long-range strikes, the Lancet is a short-range weapon intended to hit specific frontline targets such as artillery, radar systems or armoured vehicles.
It is worth noting that social networks have circulated claims of a variant called Lancet XXL, with a warhead equivalent to 20 kilograms of TNT and a range of 200 kilometres, powered by an internal combustion engine instead of the usual electric motor.
However, this version has not been officially confirmed either by ZALA Aero or by the Russian Defence Ministry.
This is not an attack drone but a reconnaissance platform whose main role is to correct artillery fire and monitor troop movements.
This is the most ambitious combat drone in the Russian arsenal, although serial production was slow to ramp up and it has never played as prominent a role as the Shaheds.
The latest development is not about range but about electromagnetic stealth. Because they are physically connected by cable to the operator , these drones emit no radio signal that can be jammed or detected.
The Russian army has a multitude of drones at its disposal and some of them have a range of up to 1,000 kilometres, which means that the CIA’s estimates may in fact underestimate the threat of a possible attack on Spain, France or Italy from the Mediterranean.
From a ship in the shadow fleet in the Mediterranean, the Russian army could launch Geran-2, Geran-3, Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones, all capable of carrying an explosive payload to targets at almost 1,000 kilometres.
